positive_experience.text: Repeated requests for labs, CXR, or imaging without prior targeted history or physical exam yield no useful evidence; prioritize symptom-focused questioning before ordering diagnostic tests.

Requesting labs or CXR in this case was ineffective because no results were available and the diagnosis was resolved through history and symptom pattern; avoid redundant tool requests when clinical history and targeted questions already support a diagnosis.

Elderly patients with GI bleeding often present without hematemesis; relying solely on classic signs like hematemesis misses a significant proportion of upper GI bleeds, especially in this demographic.

Gradual worsening of shortness of breath from exertion to rest, combined with cough producing yellow sputum and frequent albuterol use, strongly supports asthma exacerbation in an elderly patient; do not apply this pattern if symptoms are acute, systemic, or associated with trauma or joint pain.

Fever, jaundice, and abdominal discomfort in a patient with known liver disease and history of hepatic encephalopathy strongly support hepatic encephalopathy exacerbation; do not apply this when there is recent trauma, systemic infection, or neurological focal signs suggesting alternative etiology.

negative_experience.text: Asking about fever, chills, or weight loss without obtaining lab results misses critical differentials; in this case, absence of systemic signs and lack of labs prevented ruling out infection or malignancy.

Fever, night sweats, and unexplained weight loss without specific respiratory symptoms are non-specific and may mislead toward systemic infections; do not diagnose pulmonary tuberculosis without corroborating respiratory findings or imaging.

Repeatedly asking about general symptoms without obtaining specific, actionable evidence (e.g., no labs or imaging results) leads to diagnostic uncertainty; do not rely on patient history alone when objective data is unavailable.
